newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Rosneft Oil head sees altered sell-off plan.
newsitem.headline: Russian Rosneft Oil head sees altered sell-off plan.

text.p: The Russian government may be baulking at a plan to sell off up to 90 percent of the Rosneft oil company and could decide instead to retain 51 percent, a senior Rosneft official said on Thursday.
"In the near future, a rather large block of shares, up to 50 percent, may be offered at a special cash auction," said Rosneft board chairman Alexander Putilov.
"For incomprehensible reasons, the state does not have a great desire to give up a controlling 51 percent stake in the company, a stake which it is envisioned will remain federal property."

Putilov, whose position at the state oil holding company has been clouded ever since a government decree earlier this year removed him from his post as president and board chairman but later reinstated him in the latter post, was speaking on the sidelines of a cabinet meeting.

About a half dozen senior Rosneft officials close to Putilov will probably resign next month, according to company sources, citing sharp quarrels between old and new managers over how the company should be privatised.

Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin, among those who has announced his intention to leave the company next month, said earlier this week the government had prepared a draft decree authorising the sale of up to 90 percent of Rosneft this year in an emergency sale to raise money for the budget.
Property officials have already said they intend to privatise Rosneft this year, in a sell-off that will be closely watched since it is of a prominent oil company.
Putilov, echoing comments made earlier by Tumarkin, said the terms of a sale could become clear by July 28, when Rosneft's board meets.

Rosneft, once envisioned as Russia's national oil company, is one of the last vertically-integrated oil firms to be privatised and is valued for its status as the state's agent in production-sharing deals and as a shareholder in a planned oil pipeline and a large Caspian development project.

Several entities are said to be eyeing Rosneft as a takeover target. Russian financier Boris Berezovsky, who controls the Sibneft oil mini-major, the Uneximbank-MFK financial group, which recently announced a merger with investment bank Renaissance Capital, and LUKoil, Russia's largest oil company, are among those mentioned.
Rosneft accounts for around five percent of Russia's total crude oil production and exports.
